subject: Re: DPA — region-specific retention & deletion clarifications
messages:
From: Amelia Johnson <amelia.johnson@finedge.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@finedge.com
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Questions on retention / residency language in DPA

Sean — thanks for sending over the draft DPA. Our legal and security teams had a few follow-ups specifically around the retention and deletion sections and how they interact with your regional hosting options. High level questions: 
- Can Redwood guarantee that customer data from EU tenants will remain in EU-controlled regions (no cross-border subprocessors) for all production and backup copies?
- If FinEdge requests deletion of data for a scoped dataset, what is the maximum window before deletion is completed (including backups)? We need clarity for contractual commitments.
- Are audit logs and system-level telemetry treated as customer data for retention purposes or as operational metadata?

I attached our annotated DPA redline. Can you confirm which items are non-starters vs. can be accommodated with a carve-out or SLA?

Thanks,
Amelia Johnson
Head of Legal Operations
FinEdge Payments

Attachment: DPA_finredline_Amelia_comments.pdf (annotated redline)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Johnson <amelia.johnson@finedge.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 13:02:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Questions on retention / residency language in DPA

Thanks Amelia — looping in Neha (legal) and Rachel (privacy/compliance) so we can respond in one place. Quick answers up front:
- Residency: We can commit to processing and storing production tenant data in customer-designated regions (EU) and restrict primary storage to EU-hosted infrastructure. Backups and disaster recovery copies can be configured to reside in EU regions for an additional control plane option; that is available for Dedicated and Private deployments and as an add-on for hosted customers.
- Deletion window: Our standard commitment is to delete customer data from primary stores within 30 days of a validated deletion request. Backups are retained for an additional 60 days (total 90) to allow for disaster recovery; we can offer shorter backup retention windows via contractual amendment where operationally feasible.
- Logs/telemetry: System telemetry is considered operational metadata by default; however, we can treat specific audit logs as customer data if you require them to be covered by the DPA. Let's list the exact log classes you want protected.

Neha/Rachel — can you confirm whether we can accept an EU-only subprocessor clause for this account and what controls need to be in the DPA to satisfy FinEdge's procurement team?

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1-617-555-0138

Attachment: DPA_redline_v2.pdf (our proposed redlines)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Amelia Johnson <amelia.johnson@finedge.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 08:46:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Questions on retention / residency language in DPA — detailed legal note

Amelia / Sean — detailed responses and proposed language below. I'm putting plain-language bullets and suggested contract text to make redlines easier to review.

1) Residency and subprocessors
- Proposal: "Provider shall process and store Customer Content originating from Customer's EU tenant exclusively within the European Economic Area (EEA) and any transfers outside the EEA shall require Customer's prior written consent, except for transient processing in transit."
- Notes: For hosted customers, we can commit to EU-only processing for production and backups when the customer selects the EU region option. We cannot guarantee 100% EU-only telemetry if certain control-plane services are global; add an exception for aggregated, non-identifiable system telemetry.

2) Deletion commitments
- Proposed SLA: "Upon receipt of a verified deletion request, Provider will delete Customer Content from primary production systems within thirty (30) days. Provider will delete Customer Content from secondary backup media within ninety (90) days of such request, unless otherwise agreed in writing. Provider will provide written confirmation when deletion is complete and will provide available deletion verification artifacts (e.g., deletion logs, snapshot IDs)."
- Notes: Customers occasionally ask for immediate backup purging; operationally we can do a shorter backup window (e.g., 30 days) for enterprise customers with an administrative add-on and a runbook to coordinate restores and tests.

3) Audit logs / telemetry
- Suggested carve: "Audit logs that contain Customer Content shall be treated as Customer Content for purposes of retention and deletion. System operational telemetry (performance metrics, aggregated usage statistics) shall be excluded and may be retained for up to 180 days in anonymized form."

4) Verification and certifications
- Offer: Provide deletion verification artifacts on request and include SOC2-type controls in the Appendix. We can also provide periodic export of deletion proofs for the customer's audit.

I've attached a companion retention_matrix.xlsx that maps types of data to retention windows. Happy to redline the DPA directly if FinEdge's counsel can confirm acceptance of the EU-only subprocessors exception.

—Neha
Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Amelia Johnson <amelia.johnson@finedge.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@finedge.com
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2026 10:31:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Questions on retention / residency language in DPA — follow up

Neha — thank you, that language is helpful and much clearer. Two follow-up points from our security team: 
- Backups: FinEdge's policy is that backups containing production customer data must be restorable from an EU region and not be replicated to non-EU physical locations. Will the "EU-only backup" add-on prevent cross-region replication for DR tests? We need assurance (and a short statement in the DPA) that backup copies won’t be stored outside the EU absent written consent.
- Verification: We will need a deletion verification artifact that includes an immutable identifier (snapshot ID or object key) and a timestamped deletion event. Is your proposed verification output machine-readable (CSV/JSON) and signed by Redwood?

If we can get explicit affirmative language on those two points, procurement is ready to proceed to signature.

Best,
Amelia

---

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Johnson <amelia.johnson@finedge.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2026 11:22:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Questions on retention / residency language in DPA — operational notes

Amelia — quick operational clarifications from the compliance side: 
- EU-only backups: When the customer purchases the EU backup region option, backups are configured to use EU data stores only and DR tests are orchestrated within EU regions. We do not automatically replicate EU backups to other regions. For cross-region DR exercises we require explicit customer consent and a record in the runbook. We'll add a one-sentence DPA clause: "Provider will not replicate Backup Copies containing Customer Content outside the EEA except with Customer's prior written consent or as necessary for outage response as described in the DR runbook."
- Deletion verification: We can provide a machine-readable deletion artefact (JSON) that contains object keys/snapshot IDs, deletion timestamps, and a Redwood signature token. For high-sensitivity customers we can include periodic signed manifests delivered to a secure S3 bucket or via a secure API endpoint.

I'll work with engineering to produce a short example of the JSON verification output so you can validate with your auditors.

—Rachel Kim
Privacy & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Amelia Johnson <amelia.johnson@finedge.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2026 15:48:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Questions on retention / residency language in DPA — next steps and action items

Amelia — great progress, thank you. Summary and proposed next steps: 
- Agreement in principle: Redwood will commit to EU-only processing and EU-only backups for FinEdge production data when the EU region option is selected and memorialize the "no replication outside EEA except with written consent / DR runbook" clause.
- Deletion SLA: Primary delete = 30 days; backup purge = 90 days by default, with a contractual option to reduce backup retention to 30 days for an operational add-on.
- Verification: Redwood will provide a machine-readable deletion artifact (JSON) with snapshot/object identifiers, deletion timestamps, and a Redwood signature token. Rachel to provide an example JSON by EOD Thursday.
- Doc: Neha will put the proposed language into a DPA redline and re-upload. Sean will circulate to FinEdge procurement for final sign-off.

Action owners & timeline:
- Neha: finalize DPA redline with the proposed clauses, upload v3 (target: Thu 3 Mar).
- Rachel: example deletion verification JSON and short ops note (target: Thu 3 Mar).
- Sean: follow up with procurement and confirm DocuSign routing once v3 is uploaded (target: Fri 4 Mar).

If that all looks good, can procurement confirm whether the backup 90-day default is acceptable or whether FinEdge needs the 30-day enterprise add-on before signature?

Best,
Sean
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
